name: Eye-Pleasing City Park Tour
description: There is a city park represented as a tree with $$$n$$$ attractions as its vertices and $$$n - 1$$$ rails as its edges. The $$$i$$$-th attraction has happiness value $$$a_i$$$. Each rail has a color. It is either black if $$$t_i = 0$$$, or white if $$$t_i = 1$$$. Black trains only operate on a black rail track, and white trains only operate on a white rail track. If you are previously on a black train and want to ride a white train, or you are previously on a white train and want to ride a black train, you need to use $$$1$$$ ticket. The path of a tour must be a simple path — it must not visit an attraction more than once. You do not need a ticket the first time you board a train. You only have $$$k$$$ tickets, meaning you can only switch train types at most $$$k$$$ times . In particular, you do not need a ticket to go through a path consisting of one rail color. Define $$$f(u, v)$$$ as the sum of happiness values of the attractions in the tour $$$(u, v)$$$, which is a simple path that starts at the $$$u$$$-th attraction and ends at the $$$v$$$-th attraction. Find the sum of $$$f(u,v)$$$ for all valid tours $$$(u, v)$$$ ($$$1 \leq u \leq v \leq n$$$) that does not need more than $$$k$$$ tickets, modulo $$$10^9 + 7$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$2 \leq n \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$$$, $$$0 \leq k \leq n-1$$$) — the number of attractions in the city park and the number of tickets you have. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2,\ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$0 \leq a_i \leq 10^9$$$) — the happiness value of each attraction. The $$$i$$$-th of the next $$$n - 1$$$ lines contains three integers $$$u_i$$$, $$$v_i$$$, and $$$t_i$$$ ($$$1 \leq u_i, v_i \leq n$$$, $$$0 \leq t_i \leq 1$$$) — an edge between vertices $$$u_i$$$ and $$$v_i$$$ with color $$$t_i$$$. The given edges form a tree.
output_specification: Output an integer denoting the total happiness value for all valid tours $$$(u, v)$$$ ($$$1 \leq u \leq v \leq n$$$), modulo $$$10^9 + 7$$$.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1575E — Eye-Pleasing City Park Tour [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
